objectiveStatus: Rendering stability and efficiency improved; full AAA photorealism and consistently high frame rates are not yet achieved.
implemented: Embedded tuff and soil albedo textures with world-space mapping, mipmaps, anisotropic filtering and filtered relief.
Eroded rock variants, clustered formations, debris, higher-detail ridges and distant ranges.
Adaptive river-aligned terrain; water and shore ice follow the actual ground surface.
Three cascaded shadow maps across 1900 metres, stable shadow snapping, sky-derived environment lighting and cave ambient occlusion.
4096 by 2048 HDR cloud sky, 96 integration steps, small tiled cache updates and separate lower-resolution environment lighting.
Spatial geometry culling, shader precompilation and frame-based refresh limits for far shadows and reflections.
Preserved four-sample MSAA, output-space edge filtering and static wind-deformed tree instances.

Temporal stabilization after volumetric fog, preserving four-sample MSAA without projection jitter. Depth reprojection, nearest-surface motion, cubic history reconstruction, color clipping, reactive actor masks and conservative motion rejection protect fine details.
Opaque final output prevents temporal depth and reactivity metadata from changing browser-composited colors. History is copied with a GPU draw rather than a synchronous texture-copy API.
Effective distant-shadow caster filtering: Three WebGLShadowMap tests view-camera layers, so each far cascade now uses the intended coarse caster layer. The normal view mask is restored afterward.

performance.method: 1440 by 900 CSS viewport, sequential Chromium launches. Standard and high-DPI valley benchmarks use an eight-second warmup and 179 frame intervals. Live launch flight keeps the day/night simulation active, with a twelve-second warmup and 359 frame intervals. High-DPI resolution is capped near 2.8 million pixels and may adapt; it is not full native DPR 2.
performance.caveat: Frame rates varied substantially between runs, including runs of the previous build. These observations do not establish a stable 60 FPS guarantee or a reliable overall speedup. Final runs ranged from about 22 FPS in the high-DPI valley test to 46 FPS in the high-DPI live launch test.

temporalProfile.note: Before the final shadow-filter correction, the GPU draw used for history copying reduced measured temporal-pass CPU time from about 29.5 ms to 0.063 ms in a live DPR-1 profile; temporal GPU time was about 1.08 ms. Scene rendering remained the largest measured cost.

remaining: Replace repeated smooth rock silhouettes and simplified settlement/landmark geometry with higher-fidelity authored or scanned assets based on photographic references.
Replace primitive people and wildlife with anatomically credible meshes, materials and animation.
Use matched albedo, normal, roughness and displacement maps with known real-world scale; current generated albedo and shader relief are approximations, not measured scans.
Continue lighting and cloud comparison against photographs after asset replacement. Passing technical checks does not establish photorealism.
Measure sustained frame times on the intended device under consistent conditions, including launch, valley flight, first-person views and storms. High-DPI performance remains variable.
